The 2019 Incentive Plan authorized the issuance of 17,500,000 shares (10,000,000 RSUs) of common stock for future grants, plus the
remaining shares that were available for grant and the future forfeited shares from grants under the previous plan, up to a maximum aggregate
of 27,800,000 shares (15,885,000 RSUs). The Company issues new shares of common stock upon vesting of RSUs. Shares for vested RSUs
are generally delivered to participants annually, net of shares withheld for taxes.
As required by the 2019 Incentive Plan, in conjunction with the 2024 special dividend, the number of shares subject to outstanding RSUs was
increased on the dividend record date to preserve their value. They were adjusted by multiplying the number of outstanding shares by a factor of
1.018, representing the ratio of the Nasdaq closing price of $674.62 on December 26, 2023, which was the last trading day immediately prior to
the ex-dividend date, to the Nasdaq opening price of $662.70 on the ex-dividend date, December 27, 2023. The outstanding RSUs increased by
approximately 52,000. The adjustment did not result in additional stock-based compensation expense, as the fair value of the awards did not
change. As further required by the 2019 Incentive Plan, the maximum number of shares issuable under the plan was proportionally adjusted,
which resulted in an additional 128,000 RSU shares available to be granted.
Summary of Restricted Stock Unit Activity
At the end of 2024, 7,278,000 shares were available to be granted as RSUs, and the following awards, adjusted for the effects of the special
dividend, were outstanding:
• 2,677,000 time-based RSUs, which vest upon continued employment or service over specified periods of time; and
• 122,000 performance-based RSUs, of which 95,000 were granted to executive officers subject to the determination of the attainment of
performance targets for 2024, which occurred in September 2024. At that time, depending upon long-service terms, at least 33% of the
units vested. The remaining awards vest upon continued employment over specified periods of time. Please refer to Note 1 for
accelerated vesting requirements.

Short-Term Borrowings
The Company maintains various short-term bank credit facilities, with a borrowing capacity of $1,198 and $1,234, in 2024 and 2023. Short-term
borrowings outstanding were immaterial at the end of 2024 and 2023.
Long-Term Debt
The Company's long-term debt consists primarily of Senior Notes, described below. The Company at its option may redeem the Senior Notes at
any time, in whole or in part, at a redemption price plus accrued interest. The redemption price is equal to the greater of 100% of the principal
amount or the sum of the present value of the remaining scheduled payments of principal and interest to maturity. Additionally, upon certain
events, a holder has the right to require a repurchase at a price of 101% of the principal amount plus accrued and unpaid interest. Interest on all
outstanding long-term debt is payable semi-annually. The estimated fair value of Senior Notes is valued using Level 2 inputs.
Other long-term debt consists of Guaranteed Senior Notes issued by the Company's Japanese subsidiary, valued using Level 3 inputs. In
November 2023, the Company’s Japan subsidiary issued four Guaranteed Senior Notes, totaling approximately $500, at fixed interest rates
ranging from 1.400% to 2.120%. Interest is payable semi-annually, and maturity dates range from November 7, 2033, to November 7, 2043. In
July 2024, the Japanese subsidiary repaid $77 of its Guaranteed Senior Notes.
On May 18, 2024, the Company paid the $1,000 outstanding principal balance and interest on the 2.750% Senior Notes using cash and cash
equivalents and short-term investments.

Our members may utilize their memberships at all of our warehouses and e-commerce sites. Gold Star memberships are available to individuals;
Business memberships are limited to businesses, including individuals with a business license, retail sales license, or comparable document.
Business members may add additional cardholders (affiliates), to which the same annual fee applies. Affiliates are not available for Gold Star
members. During fiscal 2024, our annual fee for these memberships was $60 in the U.S. and varies in other countries. All paid memberships
include a free household card.
Paid members (except affiliates) were eligible to upgrade to an Executive membership in the U.S., for an additional annual fee of $60. Executive
memberships are also available in Canada, Mexico, the U.K., Japan, Korea, Taiwan, and Australia, for which the additional fee varies. Executive
members earn a 2% reward on qualified purchases (generally up to a maximum reward of $1,000 per year), redeemable at Costco warehouses.
The sales penetration of Executive members represented approximately 73.3% of worldwide net sales in 2024.
Our member renewal rate was 92.9% in the U.S. and Canada and 90.5% worldwide at the end of 2024. The majority of members renew within
six months following their renewal date. Our renewal rate, which excludes affiliates of Business members, is a trailing calculation that captures
renewals during the period seven to eighteen months prior to the reporting date. Our membership counts include active memberships as well as
memberships that have not renewed within the 12 months prior to the reporting date.

Goodwill represents the excess of acquisition cost over the fair value of the net assets acquired and is not subject to amortization. The Company
reviews goodwill annually in the fourth quarter for impairment or when circumstances indicate carrying value may exceed the fair value. This
evaluation is performed at the reporting unit level. If a qualitative assessment indicates that it is more likely than not that the fair value is less
than carrying value, a quantitative analysis is completed using either the income or market approach, or a combination of both. The income
approach estimates fair value based on expected discounted future cash flows, while the market approach uses comparable public companies
and transactions to develop metrics to be applied to historical and expected future operating results.

The Company is currently under audit by several jurisdictions in the United States and abroad. Some audits may conclude in the next 12
months, and the unrecognized tax benefits recorded in relation to the audits may differ from actual settlement amounts. It is not practical to
estimate the effect, if any, of any amount of such change during the next 12 months to previously recorded uncertain tax positions in connection

To determine the EV/EBITDA ratio for 2024, we need to calculate Enterprise Value (EV) and EBITDA. Here's how:

**Enterprise Value (EV)**

* **Market Value of Equity:** We can estimate this using the Total Equity from the Consolidated Balance Sheets for 2024:
  * Total Equity = $23,622 million
* **Total Debt:** We need to calculate total debt by adding short-term and long-term debt. From the Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows:
  * Short-term borrowings = $928 + $920 (2024) - $920 (2023)  = $928 million
  * Long-term debt, excluding current portion = $5,794 million (2024)
* **Total Debt:** Total debt = Short-term borrowings + Long-term debt, excluding current portion = $928 million + $5,794 million = $6,722 million
* **Enterprise Value (EV):** EV = Market Value of Equity + Total Debt - Excess Cash
  * From the Consolidated Balance Sheets:
    * Excess Cash = Cash and cash equivalents = $9,906 million
  * EV = $23,622 million + $6,722 million - $9,906 million = $20,438 million

**EBITDA**

* **Income Before Income Taxes (IBIT):** We can use this directly from the Consolidated Statements of Income:
  * IBIT for 2024 = $9,740 million
* **Depreciation and Amortization (D&A):** We need to calculate this using the Depreciation and Amortization expenses:
  * D&A for 2024 = $2,237 million
* **EBITDA:** EBITDA = IBIT + D&A = $9,740 million + $2,237 million = $11,977 million

**EV/EBITDA Ratio**

* EV/EBITDA Ratio = Enterprise Value / EBITDA
* EV/EBITDA Ratio = $20,438 million / $11,977 million ≈ 1.71

To calculate Enterprise Value (EV) for Costco Wholesale Corporation as of September 1, 2024, we need to follow these steps:

1. **Market Value of Equity (MVE):**
   - From the Consolidated Balance Sheets, Total Equity is $23,622 million. This is the MVE.

2. **Total Debt:**
   - Long-term debt, excluding current portion: $5,794 million
   - Short-term borrowings are immaterial at the end of 2024 and 2023.

3. **Total Cash and Cash Equivalents:**
   - Cash and cash equivalents: $9,906 million

4. **Calculate Enterprise Value (EV):**
   EV = MVE + Total Debt - Total Cash and Cash Equivalents

First, calculate the total debt by adding long-term debt to short-term borrowings (since they are immaterial):
Total Debt = $5,794 million (long-term debt) + 0 (short-term borrowings) = $5,794 million

Now, subtract Total Cash and Cash Equivalents:
Total Debt - Total Cash and Cash Equivalents = $5,794 million - $9,906 million = -$4,112 million (This indicates a significant amount of cash on hand compared to debt)

Finally, add the MVE:
EV = MVE + Total Debt - Total Cash and Cash Equivalents
EV = $23,622 million + $5,794 million - $9,906 million
EV = $19,510 million

So, the Enterprise Value for Costco Wholesale Corporation as of September 1, 2024, is **$19,510 million**.

To determine the Equity Value in 2024, we need to consider the given Enterprise Value (EV) of $420 billion and the assumption that the only non-operating asset not factored into EV is excess cash. We also need to use the information provided in the Consolidated Balance Sheets and other relevant sections.

First, let's calculate the Total Equity as of September 1, 2024:

Total Equity = Common Stock + Additional Paid-in Capital + Accumulated Other Comprehensive Loss + Retained Earnings
Total Equity = $2 + $7,829 + ($1,828) + $17,619
Total Equity = $23,622 (as reported in the Consolidated Balance Sheets)

Now, we can calculate the Excess Cash by subtracting Total Current Liabilities and Other Long-Term Assets from Total Current Assets:

Excess Cash = Total Current Assets - Total Current Liabilities - Other Long-Term Assets
Excess Cash = $34,246 (Total Current Assets) - $35,464 (Total Current Liabilities) - $3,936 (Other Long-Term Assets)
Excess Cash = $-788.8 million

Since we are looking for Equity Value, we can set up the equation:

Equity Value = Total Equity + Excess Cash
Equity Value = $23,622 (Total Equity) + (-$788.8 million)
Equity Value = $16,833.2 billion or $16,833.20 million

Note: The Enterprise Value is typically calculated as Total Debt + Total Equity - Excess Cash, but in this case, we are given the EV and need to work backwards to find Equity Value.

Therefore, the Equity Value in 2024 is $16,833.20 million or approximately $16.8 billion (rounded to the nearest billion).

The 2019 Incentive Plan authorized the issuance of 17,500,000 shares (10,000,000 RSUs) of common stock for future grants, plus the
remaining shares that were available for grant and the future forfeited shares from grants under the previous plan, up to a maximum aggregate
of 27,800,000 shares (15,885,000 RSUs). The Company issues new shares of common stock upon vesting of RSUs. Shares for vested RSUs
are generally delivered to participants annually, net of shares withheld for taxes.
As required by the 2019 Incentive Plan, in conjunction with the 2024 special dividend, the number of shares subject to outstanding RSUs was
increased on the dividend record date to preserve their value. They were adjusted by multiplying the number of outstanding shares by a factor of
1.018, representing the ratio of the Nasdaq closing price of $674.62 on December 26, 2023, which was the last trading day immediately prior to
the ex-dividend date, to the Nasdaq opening price of $662.70 on the ex-dividend date, December 27, 2023. The outstanding RSUs increased by
approximately 52,000. The adjustment did not result in additional stock-based compensation expense, as the fair value of the awards did not
change. As further required by the 2019 Incentive Plan, the maximum number of shares issuable under the plan was proportionally adjusted,
which resulted in an additional 128,000 RSU shares available to be granted.

Long-Term Debt
The Company's long-term debt consists primarily of Senior Notes, described below. The Company at its option may redeem the Senior Notes at
any time, in whole or in part, at a redemption price plus accrued interest. The redemption price is equal to the greater of 100% of the principal
amount or the sum of the present value of the remaining scheduled payments of principal and interest to maturity. Additionally, upon certain
events, a holder has the right to require a repurchase at a price of 101% of the principal amount plus accrued and unpaid interest. Interest on all
outstanding long-term debt is payable semi-annually. The estimated fair value of Senior Notes is valued using Level 2 inputs.
Other long-term debt consists of Guaranteed Senior Notes issued by the Company's Japanese subsidiary, valued using Level 3 inputs. In
November 2023, the Company’s Japan subsidiary issued four Guaranteed Senior Notes, totaling approximately $500, at fixed interest rates
ranging from 1.400% to 2.120%. Interest is payable semi-annually, and maturity dates range from November 7, 2033, to November 7, 2043. In
July 2024, the Japanese subsidiary repaid $77 of its Guaranteed Senior Notes.
On May 18, 2024, the Company paid the $1,000 outstanding principal balance and interest on the 2.750% Senior Notes using cash and cash
equivalents and short-term investments.

   - EBIT is calculated by taking Net Income (before non-controlling interests) and adding back Interest Expense and Income Tax Expense.

   From the "Income Statement" section, we have:

   - Interest expense (169) million
   - Interest income and other, net 624 million

   Now, calculate the statutory tax on adjusted EBIT:
   - Statutory tax on EBIT = EBIT * Statutory tax rate
   - Statutory tax on EBIT = $8,150 * 0.244 = **$1,973.8 million**

amount or the sum of the present value of the remaining scheduled payments of principal and interest to maturity. Additionally, upon certain
events, a holder has the right to require a repurchase at a price of 101% of the principal amount plus accrued and unpaid interest. Interest on all
outstanding long-term debt is payable semi-annually. The estimated fair value of Senior Notes is valued using Level 2 inputs.

The 2019 Incentive Plan authorized the issuance of 17,500,000 shares (10,000,000 RSUs) of common stock for future grants, plus the
remaining shares that were available for grant and the future forfeited shares from grants under the previous plan, up to a maximum aggregate
of 27,800,000 shares (15,885,000 RSUs). The Company issues new shares of common stock upon vesting of RSUs. Shares for vested RSUs
are generally delivered to participants annually, net of shares withheld for taxes.
As required by the 2019 Incentive Plan, in conjunction with the 2024 special dividend, the number of shares subject to outstanding RSUs was
increased on the dividend record date to preserve their value. They were adjusted by multiplying the number of outstanding shares by a factor of
1.018, representing the ratio of the Nasdaq closing price of $674.62 on December 26, 2023, which was the last trading day immediately prior to
the ex-dividend date, to the Nasdaq opening price of $662.70 on the ex-dividend date, December 27, 2023. The outstanding RSUs increased by
approximately 52,000. The adjustment did not result in additional stock-based compensation expense, as the fair value of the awards did not
change. As further required by the 2019 Incentive Plan, the maximum number of shares issuable under the plan was proportionally adjusted,
which resulted in an additional 128,000 RSU shares available to be granted.

Long-Term Debt
The Company's long-term debt consists primarily of Senior Notes, described below. The Company at its option may redeem the Senior Notes at
any time, in whole or in part, at a redemption price plus accrued interest. The redemption price is equal to the greater of 100% of the principal
amount or the sum of the present value of the remaining scheduled payments of principal and interest to maturity. Additionally, upon certain
events, a holder has the right to require a repurchase at a price of 101% of the principal amount plus accrued and unpaid interest. Interest on all
outstanding long-term debt is payable semi-annually. The estimated fair value of Senior Notes is valued using Level 2 inputs.
Other long-term debt consists of Guaranteed Senior Notes issued by the Company's Japanese subsidiary, valued using Level 3 inputs. In
November 2023, the Company’s Japan subsidiary issued four Guaranteed Senior Notes, totaling approximately $500, at fixed interest rates
ranging from 1.400% to 2.120%. Interest is payable semi-annually, and maturity dates range from November 7, 2033, to November 7, 2043. In
July 2024, the Japanese subsidiary repaid $77 of its Guaranteed Senior Notes.
On May 18, 2024, the Company paid the $1,000 outstanding principal balance and interest on the 2.750% Senior Notes using cash and cash
equivalents and short-term investments.

renewals during the period seven to eighteen months prior to the reporting date. Our membership counts include active memberships as well as

reviews goodwill annually in the fourth quarter for impairment or when circumstances indicate carrying value may exceed the fair value. This

approach estimates fair value based on expected discounted future cash flows, while the market approach uses comparable public companies

the impact of one less week of sales in 2024. Lower gasoline prices negatively impacted net sales by $917, or 39 basis points, compared to

by approximately $474, 20 basis points, compared to 2023, attributable to our Canadian and Other International operations.

To calculate the Unlevered Beta for Costco Wholesale Corporation (Costco) as of 2024, we need to follow these steps:

1. **Determine the Market Return**: The market return is not explicitly provided in the question, but we can assume it based on the context. Given that the 10-year Treasury rate is mentioned at 4.617%, and assuming a typical investment grade corporate bond yield of around 5-6% above the Treasury rate, the Market Return could be estimated as 9-11%. For this calculation, we will use the upper end of the range: Market Return = 11%.

2. **Determine the Cost of Debt**: The Cost of Debt is provided in the question as 6%.

3. **Calculate the Levered Beta**: To find the Unlevered Beta, we need to calculate the Levered Beta first using the following formula:
   $$ \text{Levered Beta} = \frac{\text{EBIT}}{(\text{EBIT} - D)} + \frac{D}{E} \times \text{Unlevered Beta} $$
   However, since we are given the Cost of Debt and the Market Return, we can use the following formula to find the Levered Beta:
   $$ \text{Levered Beta} = \frac{\text{Market Return}}{\text{Cost of Debt} + \text{Market Return}} $$
   Plugging in the values:
   $$ \text{Levered Beta} = \frac{11\%}{6\% + 11\%} = \frac{0.11}{0.17} = 0.647 $$

4. **Calculate the Unlevered Beta**: The Unlevered Beta can be calculated using the following formula:
   $$ \text{Unlevered Beta} = \frac{\text{Levered Beta}}{(\text{EBIT} - D)} + \frac{D}{E} \times \text{Unlevered Beta} $$

   Since we don't have the EBIT, D, and E values for 2024, we can use the formula:
   $$ \text{Unlevered Beta} = \frac{\text{Market Return}}{(\text{Cost of Debt} + (\text{Market Return})^2 - 1)} $$

   However, a more straightforward approach is to recognize that the relationship between Levered and Unlevered Beta can be approximated as:
   $$ \text{Unlevered Beta} = \text{Levered Beta} - \frac{\text{Cost of Debt}}{\text{Market Return} + \text{Cost of Debt}} $$

   Plugging in the values:
   $$ \text{Unlevered Beta} = 0.647 - \frac{0.06}{0.11 + 0.06} = 0.647 - 0.532 = 0.115 $$

Therefore, the Unlevered Beta for Costco Wholesale Corporation (Costco) as of 2024 is approximately **0.115**.

To calculate the Return on Invested Capital (ROIC) for 2024, we need to use the following formula:

ROIC = Net Operating Profit After Taxes (NOPAT) / Average Invested Capital

First, let's calculate NOPAT:

1. Calculate Earnings Before Interest and Taxes (EBIT):
   - EBIT = Operating Income + Other Income (Expense) - Interest Expense
2. Adjust EBIT for taxes:
   - NOPAT = EBIT * (1 - Tax Rate)

From the provided data, we can calculate EBIT as follows:
- EBIT = $9,285 (Operating Income) + $624 (Interest income and other, net) - $169 (Interest expense) = $9,740

Now, let's calculate NOPAT:
- Tax Rate = Provision for income taxes / Net income including noncontrolling interests = 24.4% or 0.244
- NOPAT = $9,740 * (1 - 0.244) = $7,367 * 0.756 = $5,524.92 million

Next, we need to calculate Average Invested Capital:

1. Calculate Total Assets at the beginning and end of the year:
   - Total Assets (2024) = $69,831 million
   - Total Assets (2023) = $68,994 million
2. Calculate Average Total Assets:
   - Average Total Assets = (Total Assets (2024) + Total Assets (2023)) / 2 = ($69,831 + $68,994) / 2 = $68,912.5 million

Now, we can calculate ROIC:
- ROIC = NOPAT / Average Invested Capital = $5,524.92 / $68,912.5 = 0.08 or 8%

Therefore, the Return on Invested Capital for 2024 is 8%.

The 2019 Incentive Plan authorized the issuance of 17,500,000 shares (10,000,000 RSUs) of common stock for future grants, plus the
remaining shares that were available for grant and the future forfeited shares from grants under the previous plan, up to a maximum aggregate
of 27,800,000 shares (15,885,000 RSUs). The Company issues new shares of common stock upon vesting of RSUs. Shares for vested RSUs
are generally delivered to participants annually, net of shares withheld for taxes.
As required by the 2019 Incentive Plan, in conjunction with the 2024 special dividend, the number of shares subject to outstanding RSUs was
increased on the dividend record date to preserve their value. They were adjusted by multiplying the number of outstanding shares by a factor of
1.018, representing the ratio of the Nasdaq closing price of $674.62 on December 26, 2023, which was the last trading day immediately prior to
the ex-dividend date, to the Nasdaq opening price of $662.70 on the ex-dividend date, December 27, 2023. The outstanding RSUs increased by
approximately 52,000. The adjustment did not result in additional stock-based compensation expense, as the fair value of the awards did not
change. As further required by the 2019 Incentive Plan, the maximum number of shares issuable under the plan was proportionally adjusted,
which resulted in an additional 128,000 RSU shares available to be granted.

Long-Term Debt
The Company's long-term debt consists primarily of Senior Notes, described below. The Company at its option may redeem the Senior Notes at
any time, in whole or in part, at a redemption price plus accrued interest. The redemption price is equal to the greater of 100% of the principal
amount or the sum of the present value of the remaining scheduled payments of principal and interest to maturity. Additionally, upon certain
events, a holder has the right to require a repurchase at a price of 101% of the principal amount plus accrued and unpaid interest. Interest on all
outstanding long-term debt is payable semi-annually. The estimated fair value of Senior Notes is valued using Level 2 inputs.
Other long-term debt consists of Guaranteed Senior Notes issued by the Company's Japanese subsidiary, valued using Level 3 inputs. In
November 2023, the Company’s Japan subsidiary issued four Guaranteed Senior Notes, totaling approximately $500, at fixed interest rates
ranging from 1.400% to 2.120%. Interest is payable semi-annually, and maturity dates range from November 7, 2033, to November 7, 2043. In
July 2024, the Japanese subsidiary repaid $77 of its Guaranteed Senior Notes.

The Company's long-term debt consists primarily of Senior Notes, described below. The Company at its option may redeem the Senior Notes at
any time, in whole or in part, at a redemption price plus accrued interest. The redemption price is equal to the greater of 100% of the principal
amount or the sum of the present value of the remaining scheduled payments of principal and interest to maturity. Additionally, upon certain
events, a holder has the right to require a repurchase at a price of 101% of the principal amount plus accrued and unpaid interest. Interest on all
outstanding long-term debt is payable semi-annually. The estimated fair value of Senior Notes is valued using Level 2 inputs.
Other long-term debt consists of Guaranteed Senior Notes issued by the Company's Japanese subsidiary, valued using Level 3 inputs. In
November 2023, the Company’s Japan subsidiary issued four Guaranteed Senior Notes, totaling approximately $500, at fixed interest rates
ranging from 1.400% to 2.120%. Interest is payable semi-annually, and maturity dates range from November 7, 2033, to November 7, 2043. In

The 2019 Incentive Plan authorized the issuance of 17,500,000 shares (10,000,000 RSUs) of common stock for future grants, plus the
remaining shares that were available for grant and the future forfeited shares from grants under the previous plan, up to a maximum aggregate
of 27,800,000 shares (15,885,000 RSUs). The Company issues new shares of common stock upon vesting of RSUs. Shares for vested RSUs
are generally delivered to participants annually, net of shares withheld for taxes.
As required by the 2019 Incentive Plan, in conjunction with the 2024 special dividend, the number of shares subject to outstanding RSUs was
increased on the dividend record date to preserve their value. They were adjusted by multiplying the number of outstanding shares by a factor of
1.018, representing the ratio of the Nasdaq closing price of $674.62 on December 26, 2023, which was the last trading day immediately prior to
the ex-dividend date, to the Nasdaq opening price of $662.70 on the ex-dividend date, December 27, 2023. The outstanding RSUs increased by
approximately 52,000. The adjustment did not result in additional stock-based compensation expense, as the fair value of the awards did not
change. As further required by the 2019 Incentive Plan, the maximum number of shares issuable under the plan was proportionally adjusted,
which resulted in an additional 128,000 RSU shares available to be granted.

Long-Term Debt
The Company's long-term debt consists primarily of Senior Notes, described below. The Company at its option may redeem the Senior Notes at
any time, in whole or in part, at a redemption price plus accrued interest. The redemption price is equal to the greater of 100% of the principal
amount or the sum of the present value of the remaining scheduled payments of principal and interest to maturity. Additionally, upon certain
events, a holder has the right to require a repurchase at a price of 101% of the principal amount plus accrued and unpaid interest. Interest on all
outstanding long-term debt is payable semi-annually. The estimated fair value of Senior Notes is valued using Level 2 inputs.
Other long-term debt consists of Guaranteed Senior Notes issued by the Company's Japanese subsidiary, valued using Level 3 inputs. In
November 2023, the Company’s Japan subsidiary issued four Guaranteed Senior Notes, totaling approximately $500, at fixed interest rates
ranging from 1.400% to 2.120%. Interest is payable semi-annually, and maturity dates range from November 7, 2033, to November 7, 2043. In
July 2024, the Japanese subsidiary repaid $77 of its Guaranteed Senior Notes.
On May 18, 2024, the Company paid the $1,000 outstanding principal balance and interest on the 2.750% Senior Notes using cash and cash
equivalents and short-term investments.

To calculate NOPAT (Net Operating Profit After Taxes) for 2024, we need to start with the Net Income Before Taxes from the Consolidated Statements of Income:

Net Income Before Taxes = $9,740 million

Next, we need to calculate the Tax Rate. The tax rate is calculated as follows:

Tax Rate = Provision for income taxes / Net Income Before Taxes
= $2,373 million / $9,740 million
= 0.244 or 24.4%

Now we can calculate NOPAT by multiplying the Net Income Before Taxes by (1 - Tax Rate):

NOPAT = Net Income Before Taxes * (1 - Tax Rate)
= $9,740 million * (1 - 0.244)
= $9,740 million * 0.756
= $7,302.84 million

The NOPAT for 2024 is $7,302.84 million.

The 2019 Incentive Plan authorized the issuance of 17,500,000 shares (10,000,000 RSUs) of common stock for future grants, plus the
remaining shares that were available for grant and the future forfeited shares from grants under the previous plan, up to a maximum aggregate
of 27,800,000 shares (15,885,000 RSUs). The Company issues new shares of common stock upon vesting of RSUs. Shares for vested RSUs
are generally delivered to participants annually, net of shares withheld for taxes.
As required by the 2019 Incentive Plan, in conjunction with the 2024 special dividend, the number of shares subject to outstanding RSUs was
increased on the dividend record date to preserve their value. They were adjusted by multiplying the number of outstanding shares by a factor of
1.018, representing the ratio of the Nasdaq closing price of $674.62 on December 26, 2023, which was the last trading day immediately prior to
the ex-dividend date, to the Nasdaq opening price of $662.70 on the ex-dividend date, December 27, 2023. The outstanding RSUs increased by
approximately 52,000. The adjustment did not result in additional stock-based compensation expense, as the fair value of the awards did not
change. As further required by the 2019 Incentive Plan, the maximum number of shares issuable under the plan was proportionally adjusted,
which resulted in an additional 128,000 RSU shares available to be granted.

Long-Term Debt
The Company's long-term debt consists primarily of Senior Notes, described below. The Company at its option may redeem the Senior Notes at
any time, in whole or in part, at a redemption price plus accrued interest. The redemption price is equal to the greater of 100% of the principal
amount or the sum of the present value of the remaining scheduled payments of principal and interest to maturity. Additionally, upon certain
events, a holder has the right to require a repurchase at a price of 101% of the principal amount plus accrued and unpaid interest. Interest on all
outstanding long-term debt is payable semi-annually. The estimated fair value of Senior Notes is valued using Level 2 inputs.
Other long-term debt consists of Guaranteed Senior Notes issued by the Company's Japanese subsidiary, valued using Level 3 inputs. In
November 2023, the Company’s Japan subsidiary issued four Guaranteed Senior Notes, totaling approximately $500, at fixed interest rates
ranging from 1.400% to 2.120%. Interest is payable semi-annually, and maturity dates range from November 7, 2033, to November 7, 2043. In
July 2024, the Japanese subsidiary repaid $77 of its Guaranteed Senior Notes.
On May 18, 2024, the Company paid the $1,000 outstanding principal balance and interest on the 2.750% Senior Notes using cash and cash
equivalents and short-term investments.

memberships are also available in Canada, Mexico, the U.K., Japan, Korea, Taiwan, and Australia, for which the additional fee varies. Executive
members earn a 2% reward on qualified purchases (generally up to a maximum reward of $1,000 per year), redeemable at Costco warehouses.
The sales penetration of Executive members represented approximately 73.3% of worldwide net sales in 2024.
Our member renewal rate was 92.9% in the U.S. and Canada and 90.5% worldwide at the end of 2024. The majority of members renew within
six months following their renewal date. Our renewal rate, which excludes affiliates of Business members, is a trailing calculation that captures
renewals during the period seven to eighteen months prior to the reporting date. Our membership counts include active memberships as well as
memberships that have not renewed within the 12 months prior to the reporting date.

Goodwill represents the excess of acquisition cost over the fair value of the net assets acquired and is not subject to amortization. The Company
reviews goodwill annually in the fourth quarter for impairment or when circumstances indicate carrying value may exceed the fair value. This
evaluation is performed at the reporting unit level. If a qualitative assessment indicates that it is more likely than not that the fair value is less
than carrying value, a quantitative analysis is completed using either the income or market approach, or a combination of both. The income
approach estimates fair value based on expected discounted future cash flows, while the market approach uses comparable public companies
and transactions to develop metrics to be applied to historical and expected future operating results.

To calculate the Operating Working Capital for 2024 using 2% of revenue as the maximum potential operating cash:

1. **Calculate Total Revenue:**  
   Total revenue for 2024 = $254,453 (from the Consolidated Statements of Income)

2. **Determine Maximum Potential Operating Cash:**  
   2% of total revenue * $254,453 = 0.02 * $254,453 ≈ $5,089 

3. **Identify Components of Operating Working Capital:**  
   Operating Working Capital (OWC) is typically calculated as: 
   OWC = Current Assets - Current Liabilities

4. **Calculate Current Assets and Current Liabilities:**
   - Current assets from Consolidated Balance Sheets (September 1, 2024): 
     Total current assets = $34,246

   - Current liabilities from Consolidated Balance Sheets (September 1, 2024):
     Total current liabilities = $35,464

5. **Determine OWC:**
   OWC = $34,246 - $35,464 = -$1,218 

6. **Adjust for Maximum Potential Operating Cash (Optional, but typical in analysis):**  
   If the company has a positive OWC and wants to use 2% of revenue as potential operating cash, we would adjust it accordingly: 
   Adjusted OWC = OWC + $5,089

   However, since our calculated OWC is negative (-$1,218), adding $5,089 would make it positive. This might not be a typical scenario in real-world analysis as companies generally have positive OWC. 

Given the provided context and calculations, the Operating Working Capital for 2024 without adjustment for maximum potential operating cash is **-$1,218**.

The 2019 Incentive Plan authorized the issuance of 17,500,000 shares (10,000,000 RSUs) of common stock for future grants, plus the
remaining shares that were available for grant and the future forfeited shares from grants under the previous plan, up to a maximum aggregate
of 27,800,000 shares (15,885,000 RSUs). The Company issues new shares of common stock upon vesting of RSUs. Shares for vested RSUs
are generally delivered to participants annually, net of shares withheld for taxes.
As required by the 2019 Incentive Plan, in conjunction with the 2024 special dividend, the number of shares subject to outstanding RSUs was
increased on the dividend record date to preserve their value. They were adjusted by multiplying the number of outstanding shares by a factor of
1.018, representing the ratio of the Nasdaq closing price of $674.62 on December 26, 2023, which was the last trading day immediately prior to
the ex-dividend date, to the Nasdaq opening price of $662.70 on the ex-dividend date, December 27, 2023. The outstanding RSUs increased by
approximately 52,000. The adjustment did not result in additional stock-based compensation expense, as the fair value of the awards did not
change. As further required by the 2019 Incentive Plan, the maximum number of shares issuable under the plan was proportionally adjusted,
which resulted in an additional 128,000 RSU shares available to be granted.

Long-Term Debt
The Company's long-term debt consists primarily of Senior Notes, described below. The Company at its option may redeem the Senior Notes at
any time, in whole or in part, at a redemption price plus accrued interest. The redemption price is equal to the greater of 100% of the principal
amount or the sum of the present value of the remaining scheduled payments of principal and interest to maturity. Additionally, upon certain
events, a holder has the right to require a repurchase at a price of 101% of the principal amount plus accrued and unpaid interest. Interest on all
outstanding long-term debt is payable semi-annually. The estimated fair value of Senior Notes is valued using Level 2 inputs.
Other long-term debt consists of Guaranteed Senior Notes issued by the Company's Japanese subsidiary, valued using Level 3 inputs. In
November 2023, the Company’s Japan subsidiary issued four Guaranteed Senior Notes, totaling approximately $500, at fixed interest rates
ranging from 1.400% to 2.120%. Interest is payable semi-annually, and maturity dates range from November 7, 2033, to November 7, 2043. In
July 2024, the Japanese subsidiary repaid $77 of its Guaranteed Senior Notes.
On May 18, 2024, the Company paid the $1,000 outstanding principal balance and interest on the 2.750% Senior Notes using cash and cash
equivalents and short-term investments.

memberships are also available in Canada, Mexico, the U.K., Japan, Korea, Taiwan, and Australia, for which the additional fee varies. Executive
members earn a 2% reward on qualified purchases (generally up to a maximum reward of $1,000 per year), redeemable at Costco warehouses.
The sales penetration of Executive members represented approximately 73.3% of worldwide net sales in 2024.
Our member renewal rate was 92.9% in the U.S. and Canada and 90.5% worldwide at the end of 2024. The majority of members renew within
six months following their renewal date. Our renewal rate, which excludes affiliates of Business members, is a trailing calculation that captures
renewals during the period seven to eighteen months prior to the reporting date. Our membership counts include active memberships as well as
memberships that have not renewed within the 12 months prior to the reporting date.

Goodwill represents the excess of acquisition cost over the fair value of the net assets acquired and is not subject to amortization. The Company
reviews goodwill annually in the fourth quarter for impairment or when circumstances indicate carrying value may exceed the fair value. This
evaluation is performed at the reporting unit level. If a qualitative assessment indicates that it is more likely than not that the fair value is less
than carrying value, a quantitative analysis is completed using either the income or market approach, or a combination of both. The income
approach estimates fair value based on expected discounted future cash flows, while the market approach uses comparable public companies
and transactions to develop metrics to be applied to historical and expected future operating results.

ROA = $7,367 / $69,831 ≈ 0.105 or 10.5%

From the provided data, we know that:

* Adjustments to reconcile net income to net cash provided by operating activities:

The formula to calculate cash flows from operating activities is:

Net cash provided by operating activities = Net income including noncontrolling interests + Adjustments - Changes in operating assets and liabilities

Plugging in the numbers, we get:

Net cash provided by operating activities = $7,367 million + ($2,237 million + $315 million + $818 million - $9) million - ($2,068 million + $1,938 million - $741 million)

Since the capital expenditures are not explicitly stated, I will provide a range of possible values based on the data provided:
